reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Meaning of levee districts and municipal acreage terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 §§ 12493, 12531, A.L. 1974 V. II p. 226 [archived Revisor citation retained as-is; parallel sections cite 1947 V. II p. 226], A.L. 1965 p. 381, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, Effective 1-2-79). Covers broad construction of 'levee districts' and sections 245.010 to 245.280 for flood, bank-erosion, and reclamation districts, plus the proviso treating 'acre', 'acreage', and 'subdivision of land' interchangeably with 'area', 'lot', 'tract', or 'parcel of land' in third or fourth class cities, towns, villages, or special-charter cities under 50,000 population.

headings.title: Meaning of owner and representation of non-freehold interests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Defines 'owner' for sections 245.010 to 245.280 as the freehold estate owner shown by deed record, excluding reversioners, remaindermen, trustees, and mortgagees from being counted, notified by publication, or served by process while providing they are represented by present freehold owners.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and history notes (retaining archived 'A.L. 1974 V. II p. 226' Revisor citation without alteration; effective 1-2-79); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked broad 'levee districts' construction and municipal 'acre'/'lot' interchangeability proviso for 3rd/4th class and <50,000 special-charter cities in (1), and deed-record freehold 'owner' definition with exclusion/representation of reversioners, remaindermen, trustees, and mortgagees in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: District formation, articles, filing, and federal navigable-stream consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12492, A.L. 1947 V. II p. 226, A.L. 1965 p. 381, A.L. 1994 S.B. 600 merged with S.B. 633, A.L. 2004 H.B. 795, et al. merged with H.B. 1207). Covers majority-acreage formation eligibility (including territorial limits for 250,000–350,000 charter counties and third/fourth classification municipalities therein), required contents of signed articles of association, plat, tax obligation, and petition, circuit clerk filing venue, and the proviso requiring federal government consent before beginning work on any navigable stream.

headings.title: Construction limit for 2004 charter-county formation modifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and Revisor footnote ('*Word "Any" appears in original rolls of H.B. 1207, 2004.' on 'The* modifications'). Provides that the 92nd General Assembly, Second Regular Session modifications neither enhance nor limit current law or its interpretation regarding where a levee district may or may not be formed in a 250,000–350,000 charter county or any city, town, village, or political subdivision therein.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections), 1947–2004 history notes, and Revisor footnote ('*Word "Any" appears in original rolls of H.B. 1207, 2004.'); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked majority-acreage formation eligibility, 250,000–350,000 charter-county territorial limits, articles contents, multi-county filing venue, and federal navigable-stream consent proviso in (1), and 92nd General Assembly construction limit in (2). Revised (1) to 'District formation, articles, filing, and federal navigable-stream consent' to capture formation eligibility and territorial scope alongside articles, filing, and federal consent; retained (2).

headings.title: Published notice, form, court jurisdiction, and multi-county scope
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including the embedded statutory notice form table, continuation paragraph [b5], and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12494, A.L. 1994 S.B. 633, A.L. 2008 S.B. 939). Covers single newspaper publication within fourteen days of filing in each district county, the statutory notice form, original and exclusive circuit court jurisdiction coextensive with district boundaries regardless of county lines, and the multi-county proviso limiting each county's published notice to lands and property in that county.

headings.title: Certified mail notice to owners and public entities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires petitioners within fourteen days of filing articles to mail a copy of the section notice by certified mail to assessor-listed landowners, franchise property owners identified in the petition, and all public entities owning land within the district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections), embedded statutory notice form table, post-table continuation paragraph [b5], and 1994/2008 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 14-day single newspaper publication, statutory notice form, exclusive coextensive circuit court jurisdiction, and multi-county notice limitation in (1), and petitioners' 14-day certified mail notice to assessor-listed owners, franchise owners, and public entities in (2). Revised (1) to 'Published notice, form, court jurisdiction, and multi-county scope' for clearer coverage of publication timing, form, and continuation provisions; retained (2).

headings.title: Authorization to consolidate adjacent levee districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12536, A.L. 1959 H.B. 311, A.L. 1994 S.B. 633, Effective 7-12-94). Permits uniting and consolidating two or more adjacent levee districts (in the same or different counties) into one district with all rights, powers, and privileges under sections 245.010 to 245.280.

headings.title: Consolidation elections and circuit court petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers each original district's board calling a consolidation election in the manner of supervisor elections and, if a majority of voting acreage in each district approves, filing a joint petition with complete election returns in the circuit court of the county containing the greatest land area.

headings.title: Notice of consolidation petition under section 245.020
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires the circuit clerk upon petition filing to give notice in the manner provided in section 245.020 stating the petition's contents, objects sought, and hearing date.

headings.title: Objections, consolidation order, filings, and existing bond obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers landowner objections by the hearing date, court consolidation order, continuing liens and liabilities, election of a new board, recording and filing certified copies with county recorders ($1 fee) and the secretary of state (who forwards a copy to the 'U. S. Corp of Engineers District office' [archived spelling retained]), and the proviso keeping taxes for outstanding pre-consolidation bonds solely an obligation of property within the issuing component district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections) and 1959/1994 history notes (effective 7-12-94); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked adjacent-district consolidation authority in (1), per-district majority voting-acreage elections and greatest-area venue petition in (2), section 245.020 notice in (3), and objections, consolidation order, recorder ($1)/secretary of state/'U. S. Corp of Engineers' [archived spelling retained] filings, and pre-consolidation component-district bond proviso in (4). Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Board officers, records, annual report, and travel expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12501, A.L. 1981 H.B. 251). Covers immediately choosing a president and secretary (who need not be a board member), adopting a seal, keeping open proceedings records, reporting work done to landowners at the section 245.070 annual meeting, and paying audited actual transportation expenses for district business.

headings.title: Landowner-set board compensation and secretary exception under 245.090
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers landowners setting board member compensation at the section 245.070 annual meeting for actual work performed, subject to the proviso that a secretary who is a board member is compensated under section 245.090.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1981 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked board president/secretary election, seal, open records, section 245.070 annual report, and audited actual transportation expenses in (1), and landowner-set board compensation at the 245.070 annual meeting subject to the section 245.090 board-member secretary exception in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: General works, property acquisition, and condemnation powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12519, A.L. 2004 H.B. 795, et al. merged with H.B. 1207). Covers board of supervisors' powers to alter levees and watercourses, construct works, roadways, and crossings across highways or railroads, remove structures, acquire property by donation or purchase, and condemn property within or outside the district using telegraph, telephone, and railroad right-of-way appropriation procedures.

headings.title: Water line authority for certain large charter-county districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Grants supplemental power to construct and maintain water lines and necessary preservation works to levee districts with at least $25 million real property assessed valuation located wholly or partly in a charter county with more than one million inhabitants.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 2004 merged history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked board works, highway/railroad crossings, acquisition, and condemnation powers under telegraph/telephone/railroad procedures in (1), and supplemental water-line authority limited to districts with >=$25M real property valuation wholly/partly in >1M charter counties in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Commissioners' inspection and assessment of benefits and damages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12507, A.L. 1985 H.B. 378, A.L. 1994 S.B. 633, Effective 7-12-94). Covers beginning duties within thirty days of section 245.115 qualification with legal and engineering assistance, viewing premises, valuing property taken, assessing benefits and damages (including state/political subdivision and railroad property), crediting and compensating existing usable levees up to outstanding indebtedness, and prohibiting commissioners from changing the adopted plan for reclamation.

headings.title: Tabular report, cost estimates, clerical duties, and commissioner pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers the seven-column tabular findings report, itemized work/organization/administration cost estimates with the district engineer, majority signing and circuit clerk filing, clerical and report-preparation duties of the board secretary under the district attorney's direction, day and expense reporting, and court-set commissioner per diem plus necessary expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1985/1994 history notes (effective 7-12-94); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 30-day commencement after 245.115 qualification, viewing, benefit/damage valuation including state/political subdivision and railroad property, existing-levee credit/compensation cap, and bar on changing the reclamation plan in (1), and seven-column report, itemized estimates, secretary clerical/report duties, and court-set commissioner pay in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Filing exceptions within ten days after 245.125 notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12509), and 2003 case annotation. Permits the levee district or any owner of land or property in the district to file exceptions to the commissioners' report or benefit/damage assessments within ten days after the last day of publication under section 245.125.

headings.title: Summary hearing, report confirmation, costs, and condemnation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and 2003 case annotation. Covers summary court determination of exceptions, confirmation when estimated improvement cost is less than assessed benefits, apportioning exception costs, and condemning needed property or materials within or outside the district using telegraph, telephone, and railroad right-of-way procedures.

headings.title: Transmitting and recording confirmed decree and report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and 2003 case annotation. Requires the circuit clerk to transmit the certified decree and confirmed/amended report to the board secretary, who transmits county-specific copies to each county recorder as a permanent record for a $1 fee.

headings.title: Limited grounds for appeal from court judgment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(2)), history notes, and Supreme Court annotation (Riverside-Quindaro Bend Levee District v. Intercontinental Engineering Manufacturing Corp., 121 S.W.3d 531 (Mo. banc 2003), holding section provides only two authorized appeal grounds and benefit assessments are not reviewable). Covers appeal strictly limited to whether just compensation was allowed for appropriated property and whether proper damages were allowed for prejudicially affected property.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2)), history notes, and Riverside-Quindaro Bend Levee District v. Intercontinental Engineering Manufacturing Corp., 121 S.W.3d 531 (Mo. banc 2003) annotation; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 10-day exceptions after 245.125 notice in (1), summary hearing, cost-vs-benefit confirmation, costs, and condemnation in (2), certified decree/report recording ($1 fee) in (3), and strictly two statutory appeal grounds excluding benefit-assessment review in (4). Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Petition to amend decree, reclamation plan, or boundaries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12532, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, Effective 1-2-79). Covers the right of the board of supervisors or adjacent landowners to petition the organizing court to amend the incorporation decree, amend or correct the plan for reclamation, or extend district boundaries, requiring a request for three section 245.110 commissioners if the plan or boundaries change.

headings.title: Objection deadline, newspaper publication, and hearing notice form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, embedded statutory notice form table, and history notes. Covers fixing a 45- to 60-day objection deadline, four consecutive weekly newspaper insertions in each affected county (first within 14 days of filing), and the statutory notice form. Retains explicitly the archived source text's duplicated notice clause ('and the clerk shall give notice of the filing of said petition and of the date on or before which objections, if any, to said petition') without alteration.

headings.title: Multi-county notice scope, filing objections, and summary hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers limiting each county's published notice to affected property in that county, affected owners filing objections by the fixed date (subject to court extension upon terms), and summary court hearing and decree without unnecessary delay.

headings.title: Transmitting and recording amended decree and petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires the circuit clerk within fifteen days of decree to send certified copies of the decree and petition to the board secretary, who transmits copies to county recorders ($1 fee) and the secretary of state.

headings.title: Commissioners, court costs, and unchanged-assessment exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Covers appointing three commissioners (section 245.110/245.120 standards) when the decree amends the plan or extends boundaries, subsequent proceedings under sections 245.010 to 245.280, taxing costs to the district if dismissed or to objectors if sustained in whole or part, and the exception dispensing with commissioners if remaining assessments are unaltered.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (5 subsections), embedded statutory notice form table, and 1978 history notes (effective 1-2-79); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Explicitly noted and preserved the archived source's duplicated notice clause in (2). Checked amendment/extension petitions and 245.110 commissioner requests in (1), 45–60 day objection deadline, 4-week publication, and notice form in (2), multi-county notice scope, extensions, and summary hearing in (3), 15-day transmission/recording ($1 fee) in (4), and commissioners, cost shifting, and unchanged-assessment exception in (5). Retained all five drafted headings.

headings.title: Uniform per-acre organization tax before section 245.180 levy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12504, A.L. 1947 V. II p. 226, A.L. 1959 H.B. 313, A.L. 2008 S.B. 939). Requires the board of supervisors to levy a uniform tax up to $8 per acre and per public service corporation right-of-way mile for organizing, surveys, benefit/damage assessments, and pre-section 245.180 expenses.

headings.title: Applying uniform organization tax to 245.140 annexed lands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires levying the same uniform organization tax on newly annexed lands and property as soon as included by boundary extension under section 245.140.

headings.title: Delinquency, lien, surplus funds, and municipal lot tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers immediate due date and December 31 delinquency, lien and collection like annual installments, placing surplus in the general fund for construction (or prorated refund upon dissolution under section 245.275), and the further proviso permitting a discretionary uniform tax up to $5 per lot, tract, parcel, or subdivision in third or fourth class cities or special-charter cities under 50,000 population.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1947/1959/2008 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked uniform <=$8/acre and per-mile organization tax before section 245.180 levy in (1), extension to section 245.140 annexed lands in (2), and Dec. 31 delinquency, lien, surplus/section 245.275 dissolution refund, and discretionary <=$5 municipal lot-tax proviso in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Initial benefit-based tax levy and emergency addition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12511, A.L. 1977 S.B. 3, A.L. 1994 S.B. 633, Effective 7-12-94). Covers post-section 245.130 recording, levying after a public hearing a portion of assessed benefits necessary to complete the plan for reclamation plus ten percent for emergencies, apportioned proportionally and not exceeding assessed benefits.

headings.title: New tax for replacing, repairing, and reconstructing works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and Revisor footnote ('*Word "paragraph" appears in original rolls.' on 'subsection*'). Permits the board, notwithstanding sections 245.130, 245.135, or chapter tax limits and after levying a subsection 1 tax, to levy a new proportional tax on assessed benefits when necessary to replace, repair, and reconstruct works completed under the originally adopted plan for reclamation.

headings.title: Bond interest addition and permanent levee tax record
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and Revisor footnote ('*Word "paragraph" appears in original rolls.'). Covers adding estimated accruing bond interest to subsection 1 or 2 levies (excluded from construction cost versus benefit comparisons) and requiring the board secretary to prepare a certified, attested, well-bound 'levee tax record' book as a permanent office record.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections), 1977/1994 history notes (effective 7-12-94), and Revisor footnote ('*Word "paragraph" appears in original rolls.'); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked post-245.130 public-hearing initial benefit levy plus 10% emergency addition in (1), new proportional levy notwithstanding chapter limits for replacing/repairing/reconstructing original-plan works in (2), and bond interest addition (excluded from cost-vs-benefit test) plus permanent certified 'levee tax record' book in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Additional bonds backed by section 245.180(2) new taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1977 S.B. 3). Permits the board to issue additional bonds up to ninety-one percent of new taxes levied under paragraph 2 of section 245.180, restricting bond sale funds solely to replacing, repairing, and reconstructing works completed under the originally adopted plan for reclamation.

headings.title: Two-thirds property-owner approval under 245.060 and 245.070
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Conditions issuance of subsection 1 additional bonds on approval at a called meeting by owners of two-thirds of assessed acreage and right-of-way miles in the district, voting under sections 245.060 and 245.070.

headings.title: Statutory form of notice for bond approval meeting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, embedded statutory notice form table, and history note. Sets out the substantial form for notice of the meeting referred to in paragraph 2, noting that the meeting will be open to the public.

headings.title: Newspaper publication timing for meeting notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the secretary to publish the meeting notice once weekly for two consecutive weeks in a newspaper in each county with district lands, with the last insertion at least ten days before the meeting.

headings.title: Bond issuance otherwise governed by section 245.230
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs that the additional bonds be issued in all other respects pursuant to and in accordance with section 245.230.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (5 subsections), embedded statutory notice form table, and 1977 history note; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 91% bond cap on 'paragraph 2 of section 245.180' new taxes and restricted replacement/repair/reconstruction proceeds use in (1), 2/3 assessed-acreage/right-of-way-mile approval under 245.060 and 245.070 in (2), public-meeting notice form in (3), two-week publication timing in (4), and residual 245.230 governance in (5). Revised (1) to 'Additional bonds backed by section 245.180(2) new taxes' to avoid implying bonds pay taxes or narrowing reconstruction scope; retained (2)–(5).

headings.title: Annual tax installment levy and September thirtieth certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12512, A.L. 1953 p. 536, A.L. 2017 S.B. 112). Requires the board yearly to determine, order, and levy the annual installment of section 245.180 taxes, due and collected with state and county taxes and certified to each county or township collector not later than September 30.

headings.title: Statutory form of installment and maintenance tax certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, embedded statutory certificate form table, and history notes. Sets out the substantial certificate form evidencing annual installment taxes under sections 245.185 and 245.180 and maintenance taxes under section 245.195.

headings.title: Levee tax book table columns, totals, and endorsement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Specifies the seven-column schedule following the certificate, matching column totals to the certificate, and binding as the endorsed 'Levee tax book' with page-top headings.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections), embedded statutory certificate form table, and 1953/2017 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked annual installment determination and Sept. 30 certification to county/township collectors in (1), combined 245.185/245.180 installment and 245.195 maintenance tax certificate form in (2), and seven-column schedule, totals reconciliation, and endorsed 'Levee tax book' format in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Annual maintenance tax levy, apportionment, certification, and collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12535, A.L. 1955 p. 601, A.L. 1994 S.B. 633, Effective 7-12-94). Permits the board on or before September 1 each year to levy a maintenance tax apportioned on net original construction benefits, certified in a separate column of the annual tax book and collected by county collectors under the same compensation and penalty rules as annual installment taxes.

headings.title: Exemption of unprotected lands and striking unpaid taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Prohibits levying, assessing, or collecting maintenance tax against lands or property not protected from overflow by district works and authorizes the board to strike such unpaid maintenance taxes from district levee tax books.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1955/1994 history notes (effective 7-12-94); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked permissive on-or-before Sept. 1 maintenance tax apportioned on net original construction benefits, separate-column certification, and collector compensation/penalties in (1), and prohibition on levying/collecting maintenance tax on unprotected lands plus authority to strike unpaid taxes in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Petition and hearing date for benefit readjustment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1955 p. 602 § 1, A.L. 1977 S.B. 3, A.L. 1985 H.B. 378, A.L. 2008 S.B. 939). Covers petitions by the board or owners of at least twenty-five percent of district acreage alleging material property value changes for maintenance-tax equity and/or a new tax for a section 245.105 supplemental plan, requiring a hearing date forty-five to sixty days after filing.

headings.title: Notice under section 245.020 and statutory form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, embedded statutory notice form table, and history notes. Directs the circuit clerk to give notice of the readjustment petition and hearing in the manner and time of section 245.020 and provides a permissive statutory form.

headings.title: Court order for readjustment after value-change finding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Directs the court upon finding a material change in values of identified district property since the last assessment to order readjustment of benefits for the maintenance tax, a new section 245.105 supplemental plan tax, or both.

headings.title: Commissioners' readjustment procedure, scope, and tax limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers appointing three commissioners (section 245.110/245.120 procedures), lifting any cap tied to prior aggregate benefits, assessing benefits from a section 245.105 supplemental plan, and applying the ten percent annual maintenance tax cap and supplemental plan tax cap to readjusted benefits.

headings.title: Once-a-year limit and recording under section 245.130
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Bars readjusting benefits more than once a year and requires filing property lists, readjusted assessed benefits, and the court decree with the county recorder as provided in section 245.130.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (5 subsections), embedded statutory notice form table, and 1955–2008 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked board or >=25% acreage readjustment petition (maintenance tax and/or 245.105 supplemental plan) and 45–60 day hearing date in (1), 245.020 notice and permissive form in (2), conditional court readjustment order after material value-change finding in (3), 245.110/245.120 commissioners, uncapped aggregate, and 10% maintenance/supplemental caps on readjusted benefits in (4), and once-a-year limit plus 245.130 recording in (5). Retained all five drafted headings.

headings.title: Supplemental plan levy, emergency addition, and benefit cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1977 S.B. 3). Covers board authority when deemed necessary to levy a tax on readjusted benefits for completing a section 245.105 supplemental plan plus ten percent for emergencies, apportioned proportionally and capped so the new levy plus unpaid prior levies cannot exceed total readjusted assessed benefits.

headings.title: Levy procedure under sections 245.180 and 245.185
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs that the section 245.198 tax be levied in the manner provided in sections 245.180 and 245.185.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1977 history note; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked conditional supplemental-plan tax levy on readjusted benefits plus 10% emergency addition and combined unpaid-tax benefit cap in (1), and levy procedure under sections 245.180 and 245.185 in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Supplemental plan bonds backed by section 245.198 taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1977 S.B. 3). Permits the board to issue bonds that, combined with existing bonded indebtedness, do not exceed ninety-one percent of taxes levied under section 245.198, with proceeds used to pay section 245.105 supplemental plan costs and refund outstanding protested warrants.

headings.title: Bond issuance governed by section 245.230
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires subsection 1 bonds to be issued pursuant to and in accordance with section 245.230.

headings.title: New tax and bonds for supplemental plan repairs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes, notwithstanding sections 245.130, 245.135, or chapter tax limits, a new proportional tax (levied under sections 245.180 and 245.185) and additional bonds when needed to replace, repair, and reconstruct completed supplemental plan works. Retains explicitly the archived source cross-reference 'having levied a tax pursuant to paragraph 1 of this section' even though paragraph/subsection 1 authorizes issuing bonds on section 245.198 taxes rather than levying a tax.

headings.title: Issuance and cap for paragraph 3 additional bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires additional bonds authorized in paragraph 3 to be issued in accordance with sections 245.181 and 245.230, subject to a cap of ninety-one percent of the new taxes levied under paragraph 3.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections) and 1977 history note; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 91% bond cap on section 245.198 taxes for 245.105 supplemental plan works and refunding protested warrants in (1), 245.230 governance in (2), new proportional tax (under 245.180/245.185) and additional bonds for replacing/repairing/reconstructing completed supplemental-plan works in (3)—explicitly retaining the archived source discrepancy 'having levied a tax pursuant to paragraph 1 of this section' without alteration—and 245.181/245.230 issuance and 91% cap on paragraph 3 taxes in (4). Revised (1) to 'Supplemental plan bonds backed by section 245.198 taxes' for clearer phrasing; retained (2)–(4).

headings.title: County collector duties, divided tracts, and collection authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12513; prior revisions 1929, 1919). Covers each county collector's duty to receive the levee tax book, collect levee taxes at the same time as state and county taxes, accept taxes and issue receipts for parts of divided or transferred tracts, and rely on the tax book as warrant and authority.

headings.title: Collector return, payment, and delinquent back tax book
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers annual affidavit-verified return of tax books to the board secretary, paying over collected moneys to the district treasurer with state and county taxes, the secretary certifying a levee back tax book of delinquencies within ten days, and collector collection of delinquent levee taxes.

headings.title: County collector bond, board approval, and secretary custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires each county collector before receiving the tax book to execute a bond (at least two sureties, double probable annual installment) to the board of supervisors, deposited after board approval with the board secretary for custody and lawful inspection or evidentiary use.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked county collector receipt/collection with state and county taxes, partial payments on divided/transferred tracts, and tax-book warrant in (1), annual affidavit return, treasurer remittance, and 10-day back tax book certification/collection in (2), and double-installment two-surety collector bond deposited with board secretary in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Chapter 65 township tax books and collector-treasurer duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12539, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with S.B. 210). Covers counties operating under chapter 65: extending separate township levee tax books certified to collector-treasurers, collecting with state and county taxes under the same bond, authority, compensation, penalties, and liabilities as county collectors, paying over to the board secretary, and making sworn returns.

headings.title: County collector-treasurer collection of delinquent township levee taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers certifying delinquent levee taxes to the county collector-treasurer of delinquent taxes for collection on the same terms, bond, compensation, penalties, and payment to the district treasurer as in non-chapter-65 counties.

headings.title: Evidentiary effect of township books and delinquency suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Makes township levee tax books and collector returns prima facie evidence in all courts and provides for lien enforcement and delinquency suits instituted by the levee district on tax bills certified by the county collector-treasurer of delinquent taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 2005 merged history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked chapter 65 separate township levee tax books and collector-treasurer collection/bond/remittance to board secretary in (1), delinquent tax certification to county collector-treasurer of delinquent taxes paying district treasurer in (2), and prima facie evidentiary effect of township books/returns plus district delinquency suits on certified bills in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Levee tax lien, certificate form, and recorder filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including the embedded statutory certificate form table, continuation paragraph [b5], and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12516, A.L. 1994 S.B. 633, Effective 7-12-94). Covers creation and priority of the lien for levee taxes, penalties, collection costs, and court-fixed attorney's fees (subordinate only to general state, county, school, and road taxes), the statutory certificate form (whose archived text retains 'not later than the first day of September' compared with section 245.185(1)'s September 30 deadline), and preparing and filing the well-bound permanent 'levee tax record' book with county recorders ($1 fee).

headings.title: Flood-damage buyout lien payoff and bond-liability cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires any entity acquiring district land in a whole or partial flood-damage buyout to satisfy outstanding liens in full at purchase, capping each parcel's outstanding lien at its proportional liability to the outstanding bond issue.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections), embedded statutory certificate form table, post-table continuation paragraph [b5], and 1994 history notes (effective 7-12-94); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked lien priority (subordinate only to general state, county, school, and road taxes), certificate form (retaining archived Sept. 1 text vs. 245.185(1)'s Sept. 30 deadline), and secretary preparation/recorder filing ($1 fee) of the permanent 'levee tax record' book in (1), and acquiring entity's full lien satisfaction duty upon flood-damage buyouts capped at proportional bond-issue liability in (2). Refined (1) reviewNote to document the Sept. 1 form detail and revised (2) to 'Flood-damage buyout lien payoff and bond-liability cap' to cover both the payoff duty and proportional cap.

headings.title: Required defendants in suits for delinquent annual assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1941 p. 346 § 12547A). Requires levee district suits for unpaid delinquent annual assessments to be brought against last record owners shown in the county recorder's office and to join trustees and beneficiaries of all recorded deeds of trust, mortgages, or vendors' liens, with no other parties required except as provided.

headings.title: Same-day recorded notice and effect on other claimants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the district's attorney on the day suit is filed to record a verified tabulated notice in the county recorder's office ($1 fee), constituting notice to all non-defendant claimants holding unrecorded or subsequent conveyances or lien-note assignments.

headings.title: Intervention by non-record claimants and binding execution sale
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Gives holders of unrecorded conveyances, subsequent acquirers, and lien-note assignees the right and duty to intervene as defendants by the first day of the return term, binding non-intervenors to judgment and passing all parties' interests at execution sale unless delinquencies were previously paid.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1941 history note; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked naming last record owners and joining recorded deed of trust/mortgage/vendor's lien trustees and beneficiaries in (1), same-day verified tabulated recorder notice ($1 fee) binding non-record/subsequent claimants in (2), and mandatory return-term intervention by non-record/subsequent claimants with binding judgment and execution sale unless previously paid in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Bond issuance limits, interest, maturity, and execution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12534; prior revisions 1929, 1919), and cross-reference notes (108.180–108.230, 108.140–108.160). Permits issuing bonds up to ninety-one percent of section 245.180 taxes, at least $100 denomination, up to 6% semiannual interest, maturing annually within twenty years starting not later than five years, signed by the president and attested with district seal and secretary's signature.

headings.title: Bond sale, separate debt fund, and deficiency levies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Covers treasurer bond sales at not less than ninety-five cents on the dollar plus accrued interest, separate principal/interest fund, 6% post-maturity interest, paying bank fees from administrative funds, advance annual levy planning, and mandatory additional levies without impairing bond security.

headings.title: Treasurer bond for bond sales and unsold bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Requires the district treasurer upon receiving bonds to execute an approved surety bond to the board president conditioned on accounting for proceeds, following sale terms, and returning cancelled unsold bonds on order, kept in the president's custody for inspection or evidence.

headings.title: Reporting bond sales, payment warrants, and treasurer self-remittance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Covers prompt reporting of bond sales, board warrants for maturing principal, interest, and bank compensation, and requiring the treasurer to remit funds directly if proper warrants are not issued, with cancelled bonds, coupons, and bank receipts accepted in lieu of warrants.

headings.title: Successor treasurer compliance and temporary bank depositary option
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Requires a successor treasurer to comply with predecessor duties before receiving bonds or proceeds, with a proviso allowing board resolution designating a suitable bank or depositary as temporary treasurer for bond proceeds.

headings.title: Restricted use of bond sale proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, history notes, and cross-reference notes. Restricts bond sale funds solely to paying levee works and improvements and legally authorized costs, expenses, fees, and salaries.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (6 subsections), history notes, and 108.180–108.230/108.140–108.160 cross-references; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked 91% 245.180 cap, $100 denomination, 6% semiannual interest, 20-year maturity, and execution in (1), >=95-cent sale, separate debt fund, 6% post-maturity interest, bank fees, and deficiency levies/non-impairment in (2), treasurer bond and unsold-bond return in (3), sales reports, payment warrants, and treasurer self-remittance in (4), successor compliance and temporary bank depositary proviso in (5), and restricted proceeds use in (6). Retained all six drafted headings.

headings.title: Appointment and number of levee inspectors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12533; prior revisions 1929, 1919). Establishes the board's duty and privilege to employ or appoint inspectors to police, guard, and inspect district levees, setting the number as conditions and emergencies require.

headings.title: Impounding stray animals and peace-officer arrest powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers inspectors impounding stock, animals, or fowls on levees (requiring owner payment of board-fixed penalty to recover possession) and grants board members and inspectors sheriff/peace-officer arrest and impounding powers while guarding or patrolling levees; retains archived phrasing 'Said (and such)' and duplicated 'shall'.

headings.title: Inspection reports, emergency labor callout, penalties, and pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers condition reports, high-water exams, board-ordered emergency callout of able-bodied men ages sixteen to fifty within the district to protect levees, misdemeanor prosecution before an associate circuit judge ($20 to $100 fine and/or 15 to 60 days county jail), and $1.50 per day pay from district funds if demanded; describes archived text without claiming current enforceability.

headings.title: Applicability to districts under sections 245.285 to 245.545
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Extends section 245.245 provisions, so far as necessary, to levee districts organized under sections 245.285 to 245.545.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Explicitly preserved archived textual quirks in (2) ('Said (and such)' and duplicated 'shall'). Checked inspector appointment/number in (1), animal impounding and peace-officer arrest powers in (2), condition reports, high-water exams, archived able-bodied men ages 16–50 emergency callout, associate circuit judge misdemeanor penalties, and $1.50/day pay in (3), and extension to 245.285–245.545 districts in (4). Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Landowner petition and board order for reorganization election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12600; prior revisions 1929, 1919). Covers existing levee districts not organized under sections 245.285 to 245.545 initiating reorganization by petition of at least ten resident taxed landowners (from each county if multi-county), record entry by the governing board, and a majority board order submitting the change to a landowner vote.

headings.title: County commission election order, voter qualifications, and proxies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers presenting certified board record and petition to the county commission(s), ordering an election within sixty days at the county seat(s), restricting voting to assessed landowners on current tax books (one vote per assessed acre), and allowing written acknowledged proxies.

headings.title: Election officials, published notice, oaths, and certified results
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers board appointment (with county commission consent) of four judges and two clerks per county, newspaper notice of at least four insertions, swearing officials as in municipal elections, and certifying vote totals for and against reorganization to the county commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and RSMo 1939/prior revision notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked reorganization petition by >=10 resident taxed landowners (per county if multi-county) and majority board submission order for non-245.285–245.545 districts in (1), county commission 60-day county-seat election order, assessed-landowner one-vote-per-acre eligibility, and acknowledged written proxies in (2), and 4 judges/2 clerks per county, 4 newspaper insertions, municipal-style oaths, and certified results in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.
